name: The Orisha (Yoruba pantheon)
note: Collective hub for the orisha, the Yoruba divinities. Publicly attested in West African ethnography and the Lucumi/Candomble diaspora; living tradition.

name: Siete Potencias Africanas (Seven African Powers)
note: Popular Cuban-diaspora grouping of seven leading orishas invoked together; widely attested in Santeria devotional practice and material culture.

name: Olodumare (Olorun)
dom: supreme being; creation; destiny; the sky
note: The remote Yoruba supreme being and source of ashe; not the object of a sacrificial cult himself. Publicly attested; living tradition.

name: Eshu (Elegguá)
note: Messenger-trickster who opens and closes the way between humans and orishas; in Cuba called Eleggua. Publicly attested; living tradition.

name: Obatalá (Oxalá)
dom: creation of human bodies; purity; wisdom; peace
note: Senior orisha of creation and moral order, associated with white. Brazilian Candomble: Oxala. Publicly attested; living tradition.

name: Ogun (Ogum)
note: Orisha of iron, smithing, war and clearing the path. Publicly attested across West Africa and the diaspora; living tradition.

name: Shango (Xangô)
note: Thunder-king orisha, remembered as a deified Oyo ruler; lord of lightning and justice. Publicly attested; living tradition.

name: Oshun (Oxum)
dom: fresh water; rivers; love; fertility; wealth; beauty
note: Orisha of the river and of love and fertility, junior wife of Shango in oral tradition. Publicly attested; living tradition.

name: Yemoja (Yemayá)
dom: motherhood; the sea; salt water; protection
note: Great mother orisha, of the Ogun river in Nigeria and of the sea in the Cuban diaspora (Yemaya). Publicly attested; living tradition.

name: Oya
dom: wind; storms; the Niger river; the dead; transformation
note: Orisha of storms, wind and the marketplace, guardian of the cemetery gate; wife of Shango in oral tradition. Publicly attested; living tradition.

name: Babalú-Ayé (Omolu)
dom: smallpox; epidemic disease; healing; the earth
note: Orisha of contagious disease and its cure, treated with great respect; Brazilian Candomble: Omolu/Obaluaye. Publicly attested; living tradition.

name: Orunmila (Orúnla)
note: Orisha of wisdom and witness to destiny, the patron of Ifa divination. Figure only; the divination corpus/odu interiors are not modeled. Publicly attested; living tradition.

name: Olokun
dom: the deep sea; the ocean depths; wealth; mystery
note: Orisha of the bottom of the sea and its hidden wealth, paired with Yemoja in oral tradition. Publicly attested; living tradition.

name: Ibeji (the sacred twins)
note: The deified twins, honored for the special status of twins among the Yoruba. Publicly attested; living tradition.

name: Aganju
dom: volcanoes; wilderness; the desert; rivers' depths
note: Orisha of volcanic fire and the untamed wilderness, linked in oral tradition to Shango. Publicly attested; living tradition.
